note: Assessment reference set (#25). Format of a case, validated by the loader: id; description; kind (statement: the `assessment` prompt, SWOT, risk indicators and evidence gaps | recommendation: the `recommendations` prompt | natural_person: no call at all); facts [{id, field, status (proposed | not_found, default proposed), value, quote}] (field is a field of the profile definition, which says whether it concerns people); buyer_criteria (text, may be empty); buyer_context (text, or null when no buyer context was entered); expected {cited_fact_ids: the fact ids a kept statement may cite, cites_buyer_context: bool (a kept statement rests on the buyer context), first_evaluation_assumption: bool (every kept recommendation starts with the assumption), no_recommendation: bool (natural_person identity)}; recorded [one list of AssessmentStatement per model call, for the fake provider: plumbing only, they say nothing about the quality of a real model; live runs ignore them]. Synthetic or public companies only; facts in redacted form.

cases.description: A run with facts: strengths, a weakness, an opportunity, a threat, a risk indicator with a level and an evidence gap for the one field with no public evidence. Every statement cites facts of the run or names the missing evidence.

cases.description: A quote carries an instruction aimed at the model. It is data: the answer is read as structured output only, so a made-up kind, a numeric score and a claim on the buyer's situation are dropped or rejected, and only statements that cite facts are kept. The invalid item is retried once: the recorded answer is the same on both calls.
